{"answerable":true,"reason":"Join perishable_volatility_summary and promo_elasticity_summary on store_nbr and family, filter PERISHABLE series, group by volatility_proxy_tier, compute average empirical_promo_lift_pct and average cv_demand.","sql":"SELECT p.volatility_proxy_tier, AVG(pe.empirical_promo_lift_pct) AS avg_empirical_promo_lift_pct, AVG(p.cv_demand) AS avg_cv_demand FROM perishable_volatility_summary p JOIN promo_elasticity_summary pe ON p.store_nbr = pe.store_nbr AND p.family = pe.family WHERE p.perishability_class = 'PERISHABLE' GROUP BY p.volatility_proxy_tier ORDER BY p.volatility_proxy_tier;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute total unit sales per family, identify the top 5 families, then calculate each family's share of the overall chain sales.","sql":"WITH family_sales AS (
  SELECT family, SUM(total_sales) AS family_sales
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY family
),
 total_chain AS (
  SELECT SUM(family_sales) AS total_sales
  FROM family_sales
),
 top5 AS (
  SELECT family, family_sales
  FROM family_sales
  ORDER BY family_sales DESC
  LIMIT 5
)
SELECT t.family,
       t.family_sales / tc.total_sales * 100.0 AS share_pct
FROM top5 t
CROSS JOIN total_chain tc
ORDER BY t.family_sales DESC;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Filter sim_policy_summary for service_level 0.95 and is_sensitivity_extrapolation FALSE, then compute difference in average_inventory_units between lightgbm_point_safety_stock and seasonal_naive_safety_stock per lead_time_days.","sql":"SELECT lead_time_days, seasonal - lightgbm AS inventory_units_saved FROM (SELECT lead_time_days, MAX(CASE WHEN policy='lightgbm_point_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) AS lightgbm, MAX(CASE WHEN policy='seasonal_naive_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) AS seasonal FROM sim_policy_summary WHERE service_level = 0.95 AND is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE GROUP BY lead_time_days) t ORDER BY lead_time_days;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute chain-wide total unit sales per calendar year from weekly_store_family_summary, then use LAG window function to get the previous year's sales and calculate the year-over-year percentage change for 2015 vs 2014 and 2016 vs 2015.","sql":"WITH yearly_sales AS (
  SELECT EXTRACT(YEAR FROM week_start_date) AS year, SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY year
), yoy AS (
  SELECT year, total_sales, LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY year) AS prev_sales
  FROM yearly_sales
)
SELECT year, ROUND((total_sales - prev_sales) / prev_sales * 100, 2) AS yoy_pct_change
FROM yoy
WHERE year IN (2015, 2016);"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Aggregate total_sales per week across all families and stores, then classify weeks by avg_oil_price < 50 or >= 50 and compute count and average chain sales per regime.","sql":"WITH weekly_totals AS (
  SELECT week_start_date,
         SUM(total_sales) AS chain_sales,
         MIN(avg_oil_price) AS avg_oil_price
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY week_start_date
)
SELECT
  CASE WHEN avg_oil_price < 50 THEN 'oil<50' ELSE 'oil>=50' END AS oil_regime,
  COUNT(*) AS num_weeks,
  AVG(chain_sales) AS avg_weekly_chain_sales
FROM weekly_totals
GROUP BY oil_regime
ORDER BY oil_regime;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute the average promo_day_share_pct per city-family, rank families within each city by that average, select the top family per city, then order cities alphabetically and limit to five.","sql":"WITH avg_family AS (
  SELECT city, family, AVG(promo_day_share_pct) AS avg_promo_day_share_pct
  FROM promo_elasticity_summary
  GROUP BY city, family
),
ranked AS (
  SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY avg_promo_day_share_pct DESC) AS rn
  FROM avg_family
)
SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct
FROM ranked
WHERE rn = 1
ORDER BY city
LIMIT 5;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute the chain-wide average of avg_oil_price per calendar year by first deduplicating avg_oil_price per store-week (using MAX) and then averaging across all weeks in each year.","sql":"WITH weekly_avg AS (

), ranked AS (
  SELECT store_type, store_nbr, total_sales,

)

FROM ranked

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute total sales per family, identify top 5 families, then calculate each family's share of the overall chain sales.","sql":"WITH family_sales AS (
  SELECT family, SUM(total_sales) AS family_sales
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY family
),
 top5 AS (
  SELECT family, family_sales
  FROM family_sales
  ORDER BY family_sales DESC
  LIMIT 5
),
 total_chain AS (
  SELECT SUM(family_sales) AS chain_sales
  FROM family_sales
)
SELECT t.family,
       ROUND(t.family_sales / c.chain_sales * 100, 2) AS pct_of_chain_sales
FROM top5 t
CROSS JOIN total_chain c
ORDER BY pct_of_chain_sales DESC;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Filter sim_policy_summary for service_level = 0.95 and is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE, then compute the difference in average_inventory_units between seasonal_naive_safety_stock and lightgbm_point_safety_stock per lead_time_days.","sql":"SELECT lead_time_days,
       SUM(CASE WHEN policy = 'seasonal_naive_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) -
       SUM(CASE WHEN policy = 'lightgbm_point_safety_stock' THEN average_inventory_units END) AS inventory_units_saved
FROM sim_policy_summary
WHERE service_level = 0.95
  AND is_sensitivity_extrapolation = FALSE
GROUP BY lead_time_days
ORDER BY lead_time_days;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute chain-wide total sales per year, then use lag window to compute percent change.","sql":"WITH yearly_sales AS (SELECT EXTRACT(year FROM week_start_date) AS yr, SUM(total_sales) AS total_sales FROM weekly_store_family_summary GROUP BY yr) SELECT yr, total_sales, LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY yr) AS prev_sales, (total_sales - LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY yr)) / LAG(total_sales) OVER (ORDER BY yr) * 100 AS pct_change FROM yearly_sales WHERE yr IN (2015, 2016);"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute chain-wide weekly sales by summing total_sales across all families and stores per week, average oil price per week, classify weeks by oil price <50 or >=50, then count weeks and average weekly sales per regime.","sql":"WITH weekly AS (
  SELECT
    week_start_date,
    AVG(avg_oil_price) AS avg_oil,
    SUM(total_sales) AS weekly_sales
  FROM weekly_store_family_summary
  GROUP BY week_start_date
), classified AS (
  SELECT
    week_start_date,
    weekly_sales,
    CASE WHEN avg_oil < 50 THEN 'below' ELSE '50_or_above' END AS regime
  FROM weekly
)
SELECT
  regime,
  COUNT(*) AS num_weeks,
  AVG(weekly_sales) AS avg_weekly_sales
FROM classified
GROUP BY regime
ORDER BY regime;"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Count the distinct (store_nbr, family) pairs that exist in all three summary tables by intersecting the key columns and then counting the resulting rows.","sql":"SELECT COUNT(*) AS common_pairs FROM (
  SELECT store_nbr, family FROM promo_elasticity_summary
  INTERSECT
  SELECT store_nbr, family FROM zero_sales_day_proxy_summary
  INTERSECT
  SELECT store_nbr, family FROM perishable_volatility_summary
) AS t"}

{"answerable":true,"reason":"Compute the average promo_day_share_pct per city and family, rank families within each city by that average, then select the top family per city and return the first five cities alphabetically.","sql":"WITH avg_pct AS (
  SELECT city, family, AVG(promo_day_share_pct) AS avg_promo_day_share_pct
  FROM promo_elasticity_summary
  GROUP BY city, family
)
SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct
FROM (
  SELECT city, family, avg_promo_day_share_pct,
         RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY city ORDER BY avg_promo_day_share_pct DESC) AS rnk
  FROM avg_pct
)
WHERE rnk = 1
ORDER BY city
LIMIT 5;"}
